goals: Quantify spun-up annual vertical recharge flux (QDRAI / QDRAI+QCHARGE) and its controls across the Naches
Validate the modeled water-table / storage state against USGS wells + Fan 2013 as an indirect check on recharge (recharge itself has no in-domain observation)
key_processes: vertical soil drainage past the root zone (recharge)
ET vs drainage partitioning under soil-texture control
orographic precipitation gradient and snowmelt-driven infiltration

model_choice.rationale: ELM's 1-D water partitioning gives per-column vertical recharge (QDRAI) once slow states are properly initialized; soil (SSURGO) and NLDAS forcing are the levers that control it.
model_choice.coupling_note: A truly regional 'recharge to the deep water table' answer would need ELM QDRAI -> PFLOTRAN lateral groundwater flow, which is not implemented; flagged in requires_capabilities rather than designed here.

answerable: Soil-texture control on annual vertical recharge flux (QDRAI) at each column
Orographic/elevation control on recharge via NLDAS-resolved precipitation and simulated snowmelt (~15 distinct precip values across the relief)
Spun-up per-column water-table / aquifer-storage state given Fan-2013 warm start

not_answerable.aspect: 'True' steady-state recharge to a deep REGIONAL water table integrated across the basin
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport and no regional aquifer; each column yields only 1-D vertical drainage, not laterally-integrated regional recharge
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN lateral-flow coupling / regional groundwater model

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation of the recharge magnitude
not_answerable.why: observations_missing lists recharge measurements — no in-domain recharge data exists
not_answerable.needs: recharge observation dataset (e.g. chloride mass balance / baseflow-separation estimates) ingest

not_answerable.why: ELM reaches quasi-equilibrium via spin-up/warm-start but 1-D equilibrium differs from Fan's lateral-flow equilibrium; residual drift is expected
not_answerable.needs: model spin-up + WTD-informed warm start (available but must be enabled)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x soil class), with validation columns pinned to wells
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands capture the NLDAS orographic precip + snow gradient; 3 soil classes span the drainage-capacity gradient that dominates recharge. Their 4x3 crossing (12) is the smallest set that resolves both first-order controls without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate on high-elevation, coarse-soil terrain where snowmelt supply meets free-draining substrate (largest expected recharge), and sample valley fine soils as the low-recharge/high-ET end member. Avoid claiming elevation isolates climate alone — pairing each band with soil classes separates the two.
sampling_strategy.replication: None initially; add light replication in the highest-recharge stratum if between-column variance is large.

sampling_plan.reason: Snow-dominated wet uplands on free-draining soil — expected recharge maximum; anchors the high end.
Rain-snow transition with moderate drainage; where recharge is most sensitive to melt timing.
Basin-representative supply x drainage combination; the modal recharge condition.
Isolates soil texture: wet supply but low permeability shifts water to ET/runoff, suppressing recharge.
Dry valley + low-permeability soil — expected recharge minimum; anchors the low end.
Tests whether coarse substrate can sustain recharge even under the driest forcing.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place validation columns at well locations, compare spun-up ZWT to measured WTD; indirect check on recharge/storage balance, NOT direct recharge validation
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in HUC 17030002

validation_design.comparison: co-located — used as warm-start prior AND as spatial-pattern reference; drift from Fan equilibrium is itself a reported result
n/a — no recharge observations exist; reported as modeled quantity with WTD as only indirect constraint

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing at native location, SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start + spin-up years

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) + multi-year spin-up enabled
requires_capabilities.why: recharge and water table are slow states; cold start gives artifact recharge~0 and default 8.8 m WTD
single-column ELM has no lateral transport or regional aquifer
requires_capabilities.blocks: 'true' regional recharge to the deep water table

requires_capabilities.capability: recharge observation dataset ingest (e.g. CMB, baseflow separation)
requires_capabilities.why: observations_missing = recharge; nothing to validate the flux against

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well / WTD observation ingest + co-location resolver
requires_capabilities.why: needed to pin validation columns and compare ZWT

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling within HUC boundary
requires_capabilities.why: expander must turn elevation x soil strata into concrete points

assumptions: Domain is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 12 km forcing applies and resolves an orographic precip gradient across the relief.
'Recharge' is operationalized as ELM vertical sub-surface drainage past the root zone (QDRAI), reported per column — not laterally-integrated basin recharge.
USGS wells and Fan 2013 provide enough spatial coverage to constrain WTD; validation column count is data-driven, not chosen.
Fan-2013 warm start is used for initialization; residual drift from Fan's lateral equilibrium is expected and reported.
open_questions: How many USGS wells actually fall inside HUC 17030002, and at what depths (shallow vs deep aquifer)?
Does the user want per-column vertical recharge flux, or a basin-integrated regional recharge (the latter needs coupling)?
How many spin-up years are acceptable given NLDAS cost (~30 min/simulated-year/column)?
Should recharge be reported as a long-term mean over a defined forcing window (which years in 1980-2018)?
